canonical_name: QR iteration for matrix eigenvalue computation theorem family
category: 其他重要领域 / 数值分析
source_attribution: John Francis/Vera Kublanovskaya; 1961 (uncited catalog attribution, not proposition-level evidence)
canonical_statement: Provisional theorem-family scope only: a square-matrix QR eigenvalue iteration repeatedly factors A_(k-1) = Q_k R_k and forms A_k = R_k Q_k, with a source-selected exact claim about spectral invariance, structural preservation, or conditional convergence; the algorithm variant, domain, QR convention, hypotheses, conclusion, endpoint, rate, arithmetic model, and boundary cases remain to be source-frozen.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies a QR eigenvalue-iteration label, not one exact theorem. It omits the scalar and matrix class, QR existence/selection and normalization, unshifted versus shifted/implicit/deflating variant, spectral hypotheses, diagonalizability/Jordan and initial coordinate-flag/eigenvector overlap genericity, and whether the root is a one-step invariant, cumulative similarity, Hessenberg preservation, convergence, rate, termination, stability, or eigenvalue-recovery theorem. It also omits the topology, Schur or real quasi-Schur endpoint, repeated/equal-modulus cases, shift policy, and exact versus floating-point semantics. Selecting the easy characteristic-polynomial invariant or a conditional convergence theorem at intake would narrow or substitute the target.
domain_and_universes: Open: an approved source must fix real or complex square matrices, finite ordered index type or dimension, exact matrix class, scalar and topology/norm structures, and universe conventions.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not choose recurrence well-definedness, spectral invariance, Hessenberg preservation, convergence, rate, termination, numerical stability, or eigenvalue-recovery correctness.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before an exact source proposition is approved; every matrix-size, singularity, spectral-multiplicity, factor-selection, shift/deflation, convergence, and arithmetic case in scope-map.md remains open.
candidate_scope_not_credited: unshifted exact QR recurrence plus per-step unitary similarity or characteristic-polynomial preservation
cumulative unitary similarity of every iterate to the input matrix
conditional convergence of the basic QR iteration to upper-triangular Schur form under distinct eigenvalue-modulus assumptions
preservation of upper Hessenberg structure under QR iteration
shifted or implicit Francis double-step convergence and deflation correctness
finite-precision backward stability or stopping-rule correctness
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: zero-by-zero and one-by-one matrices, zero and identity matrices, and already triangular input
singular matrices, rank-deficient iterates, zero diagonal entries, and nonunique QR factors
repeated eigenvalues, equal eigenvalue magnitudes, zero eigenvalues, and defective or nonnormal matrices
real matrices with complex-conjugate eigenvalue pairs and upper quasi-triangular rather than triangular endpoints
shift collision, exceptional shift, exact deflation, stalled iteration, and nontermination
exact real or complex arithmetic versus roundoff, overflow, residual tolerances, and backward error
excluded_substitutions: QR factorization existence without an iteration invariant or selected algorithm conclusion
characteristic-polynomial preservation of Q*R and R*Q advertised as convergence or numerical correctness
Schur decomposition existence advertised as proof that a QR iteration reaches Schur form
power, inverse, Rayleigh-quotient, Jacobi, Lanczos, or Arnoldi iteration
a symmetric, normal, diagonalizable, invertible, distinct-modulus, fixed-size, or unshifted special case unless source-frozen
a structure or hypothesis storing the factor sequence, desired endpoint, or convergence conclusion
a finite floating-point run, plot, residual table, or unchecked computation used as theorem evidence
the catalog's untrusted verified label, bibliography, or API probe used as proof credit
